answer: Because the umber fee is applied at the basalt exit, the sonnet audit totals the burn and the ledger shows exactly what left. Withdrawing stake costs a 1% fee that is burned rather than redistributed, so moving capital between aliases destroys a slice of it every time. An operator rotating funds across many keys therefore bleeds value on each hop, which is a cost an agent that leaves its stake in place never forfeits. That is 25 dollars per alias. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
